title: Gemcitabine + docetaxel bladder treatment
indication_text: High-risk NMIBC unresponsive to BCG, or intolerant of/ineligible for intravesical BCG.
purpose: Treat selected high-risk bladder cancer when BCG has not worked, cannot be tolerated or is unsuitable.
schedule_label: Six weekly instillations · selected monthly maintenance
schedule_summary: Both medicines are given at each weekly induction visit for six weeks. Selected patients then receive treatment monthly for 18 months, beginning six weeks after the final induction dose. Maintenance depends on response and tolerability; it is not automatic.
administration_text: Gemcitabine1000 mg in50 mL is instilled through a urinary catheter and held for 60 minutes, then drained. Docetaxel40 mg in50 mL follows and is held for 60 minutes. The team may use90-minute dwell times. These are fixed bladder doses, not intravenous doses based on body size.
monitoring_summary: Before treatment, urine dipstick and symptom assessment help check for infection; symptoms require urology review. Response assessment determines maintenance. If disease-free, cystoscopy with cytology is usually every three months for two years.

agents.name: Gemcitabine in the bladder
agents.mechanism: Interferes with DNA copying in bladder-lining cells
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine is placed directly in the bladder, held there and drained before docetaxel. Local treatment limits exposure elsewhere but does not guarantee that systemic effects cannot occur.
risks: Bladder irritation, urgency, frequent or painful urination, blood or tissue in urine
Urinary infection and catheter discomfort or injury
Nausea and tiredness; allergy or systemic effects can occur
Rare severe bladder injury or lasting reduction in bladder capacity
agents.watch: Report fever, persistent bleeding, severe pain or inability to pass urine.

agents.name: Docetaxel in the bladder
agents.mechanism: Disrupts the cell machinery needed for division
agents.explanation: Docetaxel is instilled after gemcitabine has been drained. It acts on dividing cells in the bladder lining. Its dose and preparation are different from intravenous docetaxel.
risks: Bladder irritation, spasm, urgency and painful urination
Urinary infection, blood in urine and catheter discomfort
Allergy or systemic effects can occur; tell the team about new rash or breathlessness
Rare severe or lasting urinary problems
agents.watch: Do not substitute intravenous docetaxel instructions or steroid premedication for this bladder plan.

anatomy: Burning, urgency and bladder spasm can occur; report severe or persistent symptoms.
Report blood in urine, reduced urine or inability to empty the bladder.
Fever, chills or sudden illness needs urgent advice, even though treatment is local.
Tell the team if nausea occurred after a previous instillation.
Report rash; breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of lips/tongue needs emergency help.
Tell the team about pain or fatigue that interferes with daily life.
New breathlessness needs urgent review. Local administration does not exclude all systemic effects.
Report unexpected mouth ulcers or other new symptoms so the team can check the cause.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm the bicarbonate prescription and the fluid/diuretic plan. The source advises avoiding fluids for four hours before and until two hours after instillation, and avoiding alcohol/coffee around treatment. The team must adapt instructions for your medical conditions; do not change a prescribed diuretic yourself.

Gemcitabine1000 mg in50 mL is instilled through a urinary catheter and held for 60 minutes, then drained. Docetaxel40 mg in50 mL follows and is held for 60 minutes. The team may use90-minute dwell times. These are fixed bladder doses, not intravenous doses based on body size.

The source includes prescribed sodium bicarbonate1200 mg the night before and1200 mg one hour before treatment to reduce bladder irritation. Anti-sickness medicine may be considered if nausea followed a previous instillation. Pain or spasm medicines are individual prescriptions; ask before taking ibuprofen or other medicines.
Review lasting effects, support needs and any line/pump removal.

evidence.title: NCCP 00894 and sequential intravesical treatment evidence
evidence.summary: Published multi-centre observational evidence supports sequential gemcitabine/docetaxel as a bladder-preserving salvage option after BCG. The NCCP regimen defines the Irish doses, sequence and selected maintenance plan.
evidence.intro: Published multi-centre observational evidence supports sequential gemcitabine/docetaxel as a bladder-preserving salvage option after BCG. The NCCP regimen defines the Irish doses, sequence and selected maintenance plan.
evidence.caveat: Observational results do not establish equivalence to cystectomy or other options. Published schedules differ; follow the NCCP regimen and individual urology plan, with explicit discussion of unlicensed use.
evidence.interpretation: Observational results do not establish equivalence to cystectomy or other options. Published schedules differ; follow the NCCP regimen and individual urology plan, with explicit discussion of unlicensed use.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Treat selected high-risk bladder cancer when BCG has not worked, cannot be tolerated or is unsuitable. This is a bladder-preserving option for selected patients. Cystoscopy remains necessary; high-grade recurrence or progression requires discussion of other options, including bladder removal where suitable.

Both medicines are given at each weekly induction visit for six weeks. Selected patients then receive treatment monthly for 18 months, beginning six weeks after the final induction dose. Maintenance depends on response and tolerability; it is not automatic.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
